title: Webb County Calls Hearing on Proposed Development District Near Future Bridge 4/5
excerpt: Webb County commissioners voted Monday to accept a petition for the proposed Binational Transformation City Public Improvement District, covering about 3,700 acres near the planned Bridge 4/5, and call a public hearing expected in February.
content:
Webb County commissioners voted Monday to accept a petition for the proposed Binational Transformation City Public Improvement District and call a public hearing, expected in February, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The district would cover about 3,700 acres in southern Webb County near the planned Bridge 4/5 crossing between Rio Bravo and El Cenizo. About 2,665 of those acres are planned for development in 15 phases over 50 years, according to Local National, reporting from the Morning Times.

The vote does not create the district, levy assessments, authorize bonds or approve a development agreement. Improvements inside the district would be paid through assessments on properties there, and the county would share no costs, according to Juan Cruz of JCA Law, the county’s outside counsel.

Bridge 4/5 has a presidential permit but has not been built. Precinct 4 Commissioner Ricardo Jaime said he supports considering the proposal but raised concerns that more commercial traffic could strain county roads, including Loop 20, while the county absorbs congestion, crash and road-wear costs without bridge revenue. “I think we’re going to be shooting ourselves in the foot by diverting traffic that way,” Jaime said.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 24, 2026; Local National, Nov. 24, 2026.
